results.question: Which country takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports?
results.answer: Iraq takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports, accounting for 10.9% of the total export value in 2024, which amounts to USD 149,621,564 out of USD 1,373,467,019 [3]. Sri Lanka's tea exports reached 145 destination markets in 2024, indicating a diversified export base with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.05 [4]. The United Arab Emirates was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan tea, with a compound annual growth rate of 31.6% from 2020 to 2024 [5]. There is no available data on the annual export volume of Sri Lanka's tea, as the Sri Lanka Tea Board's dataset has no usable annual observations [1].

results.question: How fast have cinnamon exports grown over the last five years?
results.answer: Cinnamon exports from Sri Lanka have contracted at a rate of 0.2% per year over the last four years, with a total export value of USD 214,425,881 in 2024 [5]. Mexico was the largest market, accounting for 38.4% of this export value [3]. Honduras emerged as the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan cinnamon, with a growth rate of 7.7% per year between 2020 and 2024 [6]. There is no available data on cinnamon exports or growth rates over the last five years based on district-level production, as no cinnamon-producing districts are recorded [2].

results.question: How concentrated are Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations?
results.answer: In 2024, Sri Lanka exported rubber to 36 different markets, with a total export value of USD 25,787,076 [3]. The largest single market was Pakistan, which accounted for 18.6% of the export value, amounting to USD 4,797,272 [3]. The Herfindahl concentration index for these exports was 0.11, indicating a diversified export structure [4]. Additionally, India was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan rubber exports, with an annual growth rate of 18.1% from 2020 to 2024 [5]. Not covered: No sourced export volume series is held for rubber, and there is no compatible price, volume, or export-value series available to provide insights into the concentration of Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations.
